data.narrative:
Asimov, a Series B biotech company founded by Chris Voigt, Doug Densmore, Alec Nielsen, and Raja Srinivas, has raised $209M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 4 private peers in Biotech & Health at Series B/C stage (Eikon Therapeutics, Colossal Biosciences, Chai Discovery, New Limit) and 3 public sector benchmarks (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L).

Two valuation methods triangulate the range. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement to the $209M raised proxy, yielding $397M. Peer-median valuation across the 4-company comparable set produces $3.5B, reflecting a sector range of $539M to $10.3B. Public-comp anchoring via P/S multiples (sector median 8.1x) cannot be applied due to absence of target revenue disclosure, standard for private companies. These two methods generate a low bound of $338M, median of $1.9B, and high bound of $4.0B.

The wide spread ($338M–$4.0B) reflects material uncertainty in stage-appropriate valuation and peer clustering. The stage-progression method anchors conservatively to capital deployed; the peer median is heavily influenced by outliers (Colossal at $10.3B). A midpoint of $1.9B balances these approaches but remains contingent on revenue trajectory and technology differentiation relative to the broader peer set.
